text: Mutating list while iterating skips entries: removing an item shifts the rest left, so the entry after each removed one is never checked. Two adjacent disabled entries leave the second in the returned list — build a new list instead (`[e for e in entries if e['enabled']]`).
Function is correct: the `n=name` default binds each name at definition time, so the list comprehension returns every name uppercased.

Trailing partial chunk dropped: `len(items) // size` floors, so `chunks([1,2,3,4,5], 2)` returns `[[1,2],[3,4]]` and silently loses `[5]`. Use `-(-len(items) // size)` (or `range(0, len(items), size)`) to include the remainder.
Average throughput is 40 files/min, not 45. Equal file counts weight time, not rate — the slower half takes twice as long, so the harmonic mean (2·60·30/90) governs.
File was 12.5 GB at 21:00 (100 GB ÷ 2³), so it crossed 10 GB roughly 20 minutes earlier.
Caller gets None: the `return None` in the `finally` block discards the in-flight IOError before it can propagate.

Script continues past the grep: `set -e` is disabled inside any function invoked as an `if` condition, so `echo checked` runs and its exit status 0 becomes the return value. `check` therefore always succeeds and `deploy` runs even when the status file lacks `ready` — end with `grep -q ready /var/run/status` or an explicit `return`.

Git behaving correctly: .gitignore only suppresses untracked paths, so an already-tracked `build/output.log` keeps reporting changes. Run `git rm -r --cached build/` and commit to untrack it (file stays on disk; it will vanish for other clones on pull).

Flagged test is genuinely flaky ~17% of the time (100 true flags vs 495 false ones out of 595). Base rate of 1% is small enough that the 5% false-positive rate dominates, so most flags are healthy tests.

Output is correct: sorting by start plus `max(end)` handles nested and out-of-order windows, and empty input returns `[]`. Only semantic choice worth confirming: touching windows (start == previous end) get merged, which is wrong only if the caller needs adjacent windows kept distinct.
